memory_candidates.content: A script that sources deploy-root-guard.sh (structural check: its own on-disk directory must end in /.claude or /.opencode) is NOT invocable from the agent-system source store, and PROJECT_ROOT for such scripts is typically derived as a fixed N levels above the script's own location (no git-rev-parse fallback) -- so there is no way to satisfy the guard from anywhere other than the real deployed tree while still writing to the real repo root. When a task's Non-Goals forbid deploying, any phase requiring one of these guarded scripts to actually run (not just be edited) is structurally blocked until a deploy occurs naturally; do not attempt a fake .claude-shaped directory workaround, and do not hand-edit the deployed copy or its output file.

To remove an ambient-environment-variable coupling from a shared lifecycle function without breaking existing callers: add a new optional trailing positional parameter with a default that falls back to the ambient variable (local _x="${N:-${AMBIENT:-}}"), then substitute the ambient reference for the new local ONLY inside the specific block that needed decoupling. Every existing call site (fewer/no args) resolves identically to before; only new callers that pass the explicit argument get the decoupled behavior. This is a strictly additive, backward-compatible fix pattern for 'guard reads an ambient variable some callers never set' defects.

When adapting a fixture-driven bash test's overlap+STALE deploy-gate technique into a sibling suite, verify the sibling's own fixture-builder actually creates the task directory (mkdir -p specs/NNN_name) before writing .return-meta.json into it -- a missing directory causes a silent redirect failure, an absent .return-meta.json, and the gate falls through to a LATER, unrelated exit code (e.g. exit 3 from a missing plan file) instead of the intended exit 6, which is a confusing failure mode to debug from the exit code alone.
